9.fluencyAndCoherence: Speaks fluently with only rare repetition or self-correction; any hesitation is content-related rather than to find words or grammar. Speaks coherently with fully appropriate cohesive features. Develops topics fully and appropriately.
9.lexicalResource: Uses vocabulary with full flexibility and precision in all topics. Uses idiomatic language naturally and accurately.
9.grammaticalRangeAndAccuracy: Uses a full range of structures naturally and appropriately. Produces consistently accurate structures apart from rare non-systematic errata.
9.pronunciation: Uses a full range of pronunciation features with precision and subtlety. Sustains flexible use of features throughout. Is effortless to understand.

8.fluencyAndCoherence: Speaks fluently with only occasional repetition or self-correction; hesitation is usually content-related and only rarely to search for language. Develops topics coherently and appropriately.
8.lexicalResource: Uses a wide and flexible vocabulary resource readily and flexibly to convey precise meaning. Uses less common and idiomatic vocabulary skilfully, with occasional inaccuracies.
8.grammaticalRangeAndAccuracy: Uses a wide range of structures flexibly. Produces a majority of error-free sentences with only very occasional inaccuracies or basic non-systematic errors.
8.pronunciation: Uses a wide range of pronunciation features. Sustains flexible use of features, with only occasional lapses. Is easy to understand throughout; L1 accent has minimal effect on intelligibility.

7.fluencyAndCoherence: Speaks at length without noticeable effort or loss of coherence. May demonstrate language-related hesitation at times, or some repetition and/or self-correction. Uses a range of connectives and discourse markers with some flexibility.
7.lexicalResource: Uses vocabulary resource flexibly to discuss a variety of topics. Uses some less common and idiomatic vocabulary and shows some awareness of style and collocation, with some inappropriate choices.
7.grammaticalRangeAndAccuracy: Uses a range of complex structures with some flexibility. Frequently produces error-free sentences, though some grammatical mistakes persist.
7.pronunciation: Shows all positive features of Band 6 and some, but not all, of Band 8. Generally clear and easy to follow.

6.fluencyAndCoherence: Is willing to speak at length, though may lose coherence at times due to occasional repetition, self-correction or hesitation. Uses a range of connectives and discourse markers but not always appropriately.
6.lexicalResource: Has a wide enough vocabulary to discuss topics at length and make meaning clear in spite of inaccuracies. Generally succeeds in paraphrasing.
6.grammaticalRangeAndAccuracy: Uses a mix of simple and complex structures, but with limited flexibility. May make frequent mistakes with complex structures, though these rarely cause comprehension problems.
6.pronunciation: Uses a range of pronunciation features with mixed control. Shows some effective use of features but this is not sustained. Can generally be understood throughout.

5.fluencyAndCoherence: Usually maintains flow of speech but uses repetition, self-correction and/or slow speech to keep going. Over-uses certain connectives and discourse markers. Produces simple speech fluently, but more complex communication causes fluency problems.
5.lexicalResource: Manages to talk about familiar and unfamiliar topics but uses vocabulary with limited flexibility. Attempts paraphrase with mixed success.
5.grammaticalRangeAndAccuracy: Produces basic sentence forms with reasonable accuracy. Uses a limited range of more complex structures, but these usually contain errors and may cause some comprehension problems.
5.pronunciation: Shows all positive features of Band 4 and some, but not all, of Band 6.

questions: Do you work or are you a student?
What is your major or what kind of work do you do?
Why did you choose that particular field?
What do you enjoy most about your study or profession?
Do you plan to continue in this line of work in the future?
part1Topics.modelTips: State your occupation clearly, use precise industry/academic terms, and explain your personal motivations using causal discourse connectors.

questions: Where is your hometown located?
What is the most interesting aspect of your hometown?
Has your hometown changed much since you were a child?
Would you prefer to live in a bustling metropolis or a peaceful countryside?
What improvements would you suggest for your hometown?
part1Topics.modelTips: Incorporate vivid descriptive adjectives (picturesque, bustling, tranquil) and contrast past vs present using perfect tenses.

questions: How often do you use social media platforms?
What kind of apps do you find indispensable on your mobile phone?
Do you think artificial intelligence will replace everyday human tasks?
Did you use computers often when you were a child?
How do you ensure you maintain a healthy digital balance?
part1Topics.modelTips: Balance personal anecdotes with broader observations, utilizing high-level tech vocabulary (seamless integration, algorithmic feeds, screen fatigue).

questions: Do you prefer reading physical books or e-books?
What genre of books do you read most frequently?
Did your parents encourage you to read when you were growing up?
Do you think traditional libraries will disappear in the digital era?
How has your reading habit evolved over time?
part1Topics.modelTips: Discuss nuance and personal preferences using conditionals and comparative structures (e.g. while nothing beats the tactile feel of print, digital editions offer unmatched portability).

part2CueCards.topic: Describe a challenging problem you successfully resolved
bulletPoints: What the problem was and when it occurred
Why it was particularly difficult or urgent
What specific steps and actions you took to resolve it
And explain how you felt after successfully solving it
part2CueCards.preparationGuide: Structure your 2-minute response chronologically: 1. Set the background context, 2. Outline the obstacle, 3. Detail your action plan, 4. Reflect on the outcome.
part3FollowUps: Why do some people handle high-pressure crises better than others?
Should schools teach conflict resolution and structured problem-solving from an early age?
How has technology changed the nature of workplace problem-solving?

part2CueCards.topic: Describe an environmental law or initiative you think is effective
bulletPoints: What the law or initiative is
Where and when it was implemented
How it works in practice to curb environmental degradation
And explain why you consider this initiative to be particularly impactful
part2CueCards.preparationGuide: Focus on the cause-and-effect relationship between legislative policy and societal behavioral change.
part3FollowUps: Do you believe individual actions or government regulations are more impactful in protecting biodiversity?
How can international bodies encourage developing nations to adopt green energy?
What role does economic incentive play in driving environmental conservation?

part2CueCards.topic: Describe a person who has had a significant positive influence on your life
bulletPoints: Who this person is and your relationship to them
What qualities and attributes distinguish them
What pivotal advice or assistance they provided to you
And explain why their guidance has had such a lasting impression on your life
part2CueCards.preparationGuide: Highlight personality traits with vivid vocabulary, back up claims with an illustrative story, and conclude with the long-term impact on your values.
part3FollowUps: What qualities make someone an effective mentor or leader?
Do role models in popular media exert a healthier influence today than in the past?
How does intergenerational mentorship benefit modern corporate cultures?

speakingFormulas.structure: While it is undeniably true that [Concession A], one cannot overlook the fact that [Counter-Point B], which ultimately leads to [Conclusion].
speakingFormulas.example: While it is undeniably true that remote work affords greater flexibility, one cannot overlook the fact that lack of face-to-face interaction can erode team synergy.

speakingFormulas.structure: More often than not, I tend to gravitate towards [Option A]; however, whenever circumstances dictate, I readily opt for [Option B].
speakingFormulas.example: More often than not, I tend to gravitate towards classical literature; however, whenever time is constrained, I readily opt for concise audiobooks.

speakingFormulas.structure: Had I not been exposed to [Event/Person], my perspective on [Subject] would undoubtedly be fundamentally different today.
speakingFormulas.example: Had I not taken part in an international exchange programme, my perspective on global collaboration would undoubtedly be fundamentally different today.
speakingFormulas.criterionTarget: Grammatical Range and Accuracy (Inverted Third Conditional)

authenticTranscripts.title: Embarrassment & Social Perception
authenticTranscripts.excerpt: To be embarrassed would be to assume that anyone in this room or anyone who witnessed this actually spends more than 5 seconds thinking about me. And they do not... This worldview, that others were not judging her, helped her not judge herself.

authenticTranscripts.title: Judgment Day & Linguistic Awareness
authenticTranscripts.excerpt: I learned from a coworker that all my life I have been mispronouncing the word incongruous. Embarrassment is on me all the time, and I want to get it off... The best stories say so much about us, reveal sides of ourselves maybe we would rather not see.
